name: Sanskriti Saraf
tested: Dashboard, vet search/no-results, appointments, records, triage screen, synthetic pet registration and reload persistence.
limitations: Booking, video calling and clinical AI output not exercised. Default relative avatar URL prevented submission until replaced with absolute URL.
feedback: The care dashboard, vet discovery and medical-record views form a coherent product, and a new demo pet survived reload. Fix the default avatar URL validation that blocks registration, and prove the consultation and triage flows with clear demo-safe outcomes.

name: Ananya Chadha
tested: Signup screen and About page.
limitations: Account required; no guest/demo route or supplied credentials. Core journal, cycle and persistence unobserved.
feedback: The restrained typography and seasonal identity are distinctive, and the About page explains the concept carefully. Provide a guest or evaluator account so the cycle wheel, journal and saved entries can be assessed beyond the entry screen.

name: Sahithi Vakkalanka
tested: Home, shop, product detail, add to bag, cart persistence after reload, Our story and Contact.
limitations: Checkout completion, payments and outgoing enquiries not executed.
feedback: The product photography, editorial styling and detailed product pages create a convincing storefront; adding a clutch to the bag also persisted after reload. Strengthen product specifications with measurable dimensions and demonstrate a safe checkout completion path to validate the final purchase step.

name: P.L.Praneeth
tested: Today, tomorrow missing-menu state, month archive, no-results search, activity lookup with synthetic room, reload.
limitations: No meal request or real attendance sent. Updating room lookup persisted a resident identity without normal login; backend guarantees unknown.
feedback: The compact meal cards, monthly archive and activity filters support a clear hostel use case. Separate room-history lookup from authentication: entering a synthetic room left the app signed in as that resident after reload, and the public demo should not imply verified server sync without demonstrating it.

name: G Naga Supriya
tested: Veg filter, add item, calculated total, checkout phone gate, reload.
limitations: No phone or order sent. Cart cleared on reload; initial late menu refresh also cleared selection.
feedback: The focused menu and dietary filters make pre-ordering easy to understand, and the selected item reached a correctly priced checkout prompt. Preserve the cart across menu refreshes and reloads, and remove the visible test item “dsvfg” before presenting this as a finished ordering experience.

name: Anushka Kothari
tested: Home, save action, class detail, search, bookings, profile, favorite and reload.
limitations: No booking placed. Saved count remained zero after favorite/reload; initial card link click did not open details, so visible href used. Details showed Jan 1 versus Aug 31 listing date.
feedback: The dance marketplace has a strong visual identity and rich discovery screens, but its detail page showed a different date from the class card and a saved class did not appear in the profile after reload. Resolve the inconsistent data and verify save-to-profile and booking continuity before adding more catalogue content.

name: K.E.Viswaram
tested: Team/one-over setup, default players, scoring, undo, strike change, reload persistence, innings transition, successful chase, detailed scorecard and saved archive.
limitations: Wickets, extras and offline network mode not fully exercised. Undo history was disabled after reload although score persisted.
feedback: GullyCric delivers a complete scoring loop: setup, strike rotation, innings break, winning result and detailed scorecards all worked, with the match retained after reload. Preserve undo history across reloads and extend the same verification to wickets and extras to make live scoring more resilient.

name: priyam dowerah
tested: Case selection, clue discovery, questions/action counter, deduction board, invalid inference, wrong accusation and explanatory verdict; reload.
limitations: Successful solution and other five cases not completed; reloading case returns to introduction.
feedback: The literary presentation and constrained investigation mechanics work together well: clues cost actions, unsupported deductions are tracked, and a failed accusation receives a detailed explanatory verdict. Add a clearer example of constructing a valid inference and preserve the in-progress case across reloads.

name: Parv Yadav
tested: Event checklist, detailed document requirements and letter workflow, custom task add, completion and reload persistence, overview.
limitations: Legal guidance not independently validated; no external filings or emails. Custom additions appeared after reload, causing duplicate test task on retry.
feedback: CareList combines calm design with unusually specific document checklists, letter templates and a useful completion overview; a custom completed task survived reload. Make newly added tasks appear immediately, and attach dated official sources to the legal and benefit guidance so users can verify eligibility safely.

name: Khyati Chaturvedi
tested: Explore, Capture & Design with supplied sample, generated comparison, Spatial Studio, Prop Finder, reload.
limitations: Camera/uploads and purchases not performed. Generated render count reverted 4 to 3 after reload; merchant Buy links lead to retailer homepages; genuine generation unverified.
feedback: The sample-room flow reaches a comparison screen with furniture hotspots, but the hero text is almost white on white and the saved render disappeared on reload. Improve contrast and persistence, then replace generic retailer-homepage links and preset imagery with verifiable room-specific results and product destinations.

name: Achal Kaur
tested: Eight-step quiz, office/trousers/classic/flats/budget/colors/free text, personalized results, reload.
limitations: Suggested top pair ₹2450 exceeds selected ₹1000–₹2000 budget; alternative heels conflict with flats preference. No purchase path tested.
feedback: The elegant quiz produces an explanation that uses the selected occasion, outfit and notes. However, the top ₹2,450 recommendation exceeded the ₹1,000–₹2,000 budget and alternatives ignored the flat-shoe preference; enforce these constraints before presenting match percentages as precise.

name: Kunal Tomar
tested: Supplied dashboard redirects to sign-in; public home and plan CTA.
limitations: No guest path or supplied account; itinerary, route and checklist functions unobserved.
feedback: The landing page communicates a specific match-day journey and the entry screens are consistent. Supply a guest itinerary or evaluator login so departure calculations, route planning and saved match checklists can be tested rather than assessed from feature claims.

name: Aradhya Bapna
tested: Synthetic manager room creation, bot auction, timed sale and budget deduction, pause, reload and rejoin with room code.
limitations: No money involved, only fantasy demo. Rejoin restored paused room but Resume did not unpause, leaving bid disabled; multiplayer clients unverified.
feedback: The fantasy auction has substantial working behavior: bots bid, a player sells, budgets update, and the room can be recovered by code after reload. Fix host-control recovery after rejoining—the room stayed paused despite Resume—and add an obvious reconnect action instead of returning users to the lobby.

name: Yaramareddy Hrithik Reddy
tested: Login screen and available entry actions.
limitations: No guest mode or supplied credentials; gameplay not accessible.
feedback: The playful login screen suits a word game, but the logo says Word Rush while the heading says WordPals. Unify the naming and provide a guest game or evaluator account so puzzle rules, scoring and progression can actually be reviewed.

name: Sanya Bansal
tested: Blank-submit disabled state, synthetic startup idea, Gentle intensity, context-specific roast and practical advice, reload.
limitations: No saved history; result cleared on reload. Other intensity not compared.
feedback: The core loop works: a specific roommate meal-planning idea produced a relevant roast and actionable criticism rather than generic filler. Add saved results or a visible warning before leaving, and make the Gentle versus Brutal distinction measurable with the same test pitch.

name: Vandit Jain
tested: Landing page, feature/demo destination and generate-report signup gate.
limitations: Core reports and exports require account; no public working sample supplied.
feedback: The landing page has clear hierarchy and communicates the proposed research output well. Replace the “90-second demo” anchor with a real demonstration or sample report, and provide evaluator access so sources, calculations and exports can be checked.

name: Sankalp Sharma
tested: Map pin, timed trivia failure, location detail, revealed collection, daily screen, premiere progress, reload persistence.
limitations: No device location or external directions used. Timer expired yet detail awarded +100 and collection counted pin; correct-answer path not tested.
feedback: The map, trivia reveal and collection create a coherent film-discovery loop, and the revealed location persisted after reload. Clarify the scoring rules: a timed-out answer showed “Cut! Try Again” yet still awarded 100 points, and repeated generic silhouettes make the clues difficult to interpret.

name: Saloni Baid
tested: Demo dashboard, business profile, opportunity matrix, context-specific AI answer, generated 12-task plan, completion toggle and reload.
limitations: Plan and completion were absent after reload. No new business account or external messaging; recommendations are estimates, not validated business outcomes.
feedback: GrowthOS turns demo business metrics into specific opportunities, relevant answers and a practical four-week task plan. Persist the generated plan and task completion across reloads, and show the assumptions behind revenue-upside figures instead of implying guaranteed gains.

tested: Demo onboarding; dashboard/products/marketing/finance/customers/goals/copilot/settings; synthetic task creation and reload persistence.
limitations: Integrations, uploads and AI response not exercised. Conflicting ROAS/runway and margin figures appear across seeded screens.
feedback: FounderOS has substantial breadth, readable dashboards and a task workflow that saved a new item across reloads. Reconcile the financial figures before presenting them as live intelligence: the dashboard and Finance screens disagree on runway, and the displayed net margin does not match the shown revenue and profit.
name: Kusum Lalwani
Saloni Baid
tested: Demo dashboard, business profile, opportunity matrix, context-specific AI answer, generated 12-task plan, completion toggle and reload. Exact duplicate URL; review reused from source row47.
limitations: Plan and completion were absent after reload. No new business account or external messaging; recommendations are estimates, not validated business outcomes.
feedback: GrowthOS turns demo business metrics into specific opportunities, relevant answers and a practical four-week task plan. Persist the generated plan and task completion across reloads, and show the assumptions behind revenue-upside figures instead of implying guaranteed gains.

tested: Public landing and wardrobe CTA to signup.
limitations: Account required; wardrobe uploads, outfit creation and avatar unobserved.
feedback: The restrained landing page clearly explains the upload–style–wear journey. Provide a sample wardrobe or evaluator login so outfit generation and saved looks can be tested, and show real product screens rather than leaving the value proposition entirely in text.
name: Riddhi Singla

feedback: The navy-and-gold presentation, clear hourly pricing and cancellation FAQ make the service easy to understand. Booking opens an authentication screen, so provide an evaluator account or a safe demo journey to demonstrate availability, booking and cancellation end to end.
tested: Inspected homepage, Pricing, For drivers and Contact; expanded cancellation FAQ; Book a driver redirected to authentication.
limitations: Core booking and cancellation could not be verified without authentication; no account, contact, booking or payment was submitted.
name: Shiven Dogra

feedback: The distinct visual identity, linked profiles and time/fraternity filters make the leaderboard feel coherent and usable. Give podium names enough room, and fix the Story action that remained on “Building…” across repeated checks so the sharing flow has a reliable result or error state.
tested: Inspected All-Time, Month, Week and Feed; switched sleeper/spotter roles; filtered META; nonexistent-name search displayed No one found; week/filter survived reload; opened a profile and started Story generation, which remained Building across several checks.
limitations: Read-only public review; did not claim identities, send WhatsApp messages or contact anyone. Administrative ingestion, consent controls and moderation not verified; Story completion was not observed.
name: Param Parekh

feedback: The image-led discovery, saved destinations and integrated trip workspace form a clear and attractive travel product. Replace the mismatched sample content: Tokyo’s timeline lands in Santorini, and the wallet repeats documents, so destination-specific planning needs stronger consistency before users can trust it.
tested: Completed onboarding and inspected Home, Discover, Trips, Wallet and Profile plus Timeline, Documents, Packing, Budget, Airport, Arrival and Memories. Saved Amalfi destination and verified Remove from saved after reload. Built-in Santorini image produced Oia identification with detailed destination information and prefilled planning handoff. New-trip date entry could not be completed through browser tooling; other fields and validation visible.
limitations: Native date entry encountered browser automation limitations, not counted as an app defect. New-trip generation/persistence and recognition of user-supplied images remain unverified; built-in image is a sample, not proof of general visual AI. No real documents uploaded, bookings made or seeded trip records changed.
name: Nitish Juttu

feedback: The property comparison and detailed tour controls communicate a strong self-guided viewing concept. Persist shortlists, make the assistant enforce budget and location constraints, and replace mismatched tour imagery—the “Master Suite” displayed an exterior pool photo—before presenting the demo as a reliable property service.
tested: Inspected Explore, Bookings, Smart Key, Compare, Owner Portal and AI Assistant; Maharashtra filter reduced catalogue to two properties; two-property comparison showed correct differing rents and areas but disappeared on reload. Opened property detail and tour, moved to next room and opened Floor Plan. Asked for Maharashtra home under ₹100000/month; generic answer returned both out-of-budget and out-of-state matches.
limitations: Camera explicitly simulated; lock hardware, screening, legal verification and actual 3D capture not verified. No booking, owner contact, payment, device permission or physical unlock attempted. Some polished tour controls operate over mismatched sample photos.
name: Sachin Gupta
